draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Benaulim! Before the Portuguese came it was Banahalli, 'the village of the arrow', and the story goes that Parashurama's arrow landed right here when he pushed back the sea. It's also long been known as Goa's 'village of carpenters'.
draft.hungryLine: Restaurants line the beachfront and the crossroads here, all serving fresh fish and the odd curry classic.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Head to the Goa Chitra Museum, packed with over 4,000 old farming tools and household objects, then check out the San Thome Museum on the Cavelossim road.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Just go to the beach, Benaulim is known for its golden sands and palm-fringed shore.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Benaulim hosted the 8th BRICS Summit in 2016.

spots.name: Goa Chitra Museum
spots.detail: Short drive · Ethnographic museum of Goa's rural and farming life

spots.name: San Thome Museum
spots.detail: Short drive · Old industrial and household appliances on show

status.text: On the Dabolim to Cavelossim road

legends.title: Where the arrow fell
legends.body: Locals tell that Parashurama shot an arrow into the sea and ordered the sea god Varuna to recede to where it landed. That arrow is said to have come down here, which is how Banahalli, 'village of the arrow', got its name.

tips.title: Go dolphin spotting early.
tips.body: Local fishermen run morning dolphin spotting boat rides from the beach.

tips.title: Rent wheels for day trips.
tips.body: Hire a bike or car to explore nearby Chandor, Quepem and Ponda's temples and spice plantations.

story.title: Village of the arrow
story.body: Before the Portuguese, the village was called Banahalli or Banawali. The name mixes Sanskrit 'ban', arrow, with Kannada 'halli', village.

story.title: A communidade of Salcete
story.body: Under Portuguese rule Benaulim was one of the nine communidades of Salcete. St. Joseph Vaz, later a priest and missionary in Ceylon, was born here and baptised at St John the Baptist Church.

story.title: A museum of everyday life
story.body: Artist and restorer Victor Hugo Gomes opened the Goa Chitra Museum in 2009. He funds it himself and calls the collection a living ode to Goa's material heritage.

story.title: The world comes to the village
story.body: Benaulim hosted the 8th BRICS Summit in 2016. Today it's a popular seaside resort of about 13,000 people.
